newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Little downside seen for rising Belgian shares.
newsitem.headline: Little downside seen for rising Belgian shares.

text.p: Dealers see little downside for a Belgian sharemarket underpinned by a bullish Wall Street, firm local bonds and a healthy U.S. dollar.
"We've been looking for a bit of consolidation, but every day we seem to be going up a bit," said a dealer. "Everyone wants to be in and they don't care if the market's not cheap today."

The Bel-20 index ended 8.14 points or 0.45 percent higher on Friday at 1,806.20 points. It came off an earlier high of 1,811.47 points after the Dow Jones fell in early U.S. trade on a wider than expected August U.S. trade gap.
Textile firm Sioen Industries began trading on the second-tier cash market where it closed at 1,620 francs a share, 220 francs above its issue price.
"It had a wonderful first day," said a trader. "With 40,000 shares traded and a 15 percent rise, I think its price will be capped about 1,700 francs for the moment."
Chemicals and drug company UCB climbed 750 francs to a new record high close of 68,700 francs per share.
"There's been good news on its earnings growth prospects and today's gains came in an empty, illiquid market with only 1,900 shares traded," a dealer said.

He said photo finishing group Spector may have suffered from arbitrage. The company is undergoing a 2.75 billion francs capital raising and tumbled 2.4 percent to 2,030 francs with more than 8,000 shares changing hands.
"The rights were down 20 francs today and it could be that there's some arbitrage going on between the stock and its rights."
Generale Bank analysts said Spector's share issue was weighing on the market and recommended the stock as a buy at current prices.
